The Australian government has appointed former Liberal minister Philip Ruddock to review whether existing laws sufficiently protect the human right to religious freedom. This decision, announced by the cabinet on Wednesday, is seen as a proactive measure to mitigate potential disputes regarding religious amendments tied to a same-sex marriage bill. Despite this appointment, Treasurer Scott Morrison emphasized that the review should not be viewed as a substitute for the proposed amendments within the marriage legislation.

Prime Minister Malcolm Turnbull highlighted the necessity of carefully examining religious freedom issues, especially following the recent same-sex marriage vote and upcoming equality legislation. Senior conservatives, including Peter Dutton and Mathias Cormann, have indicated that a standalone religious freedom bill could be deliberated next year, separate from marriage legislation. However, some, including Morrison and Liberal senator David Fawcett, advocate for addressing both issues concurrently.

Ruddock has been tasked with presenting his findings by March 31. Turnbull noted that various proposals for legal protections for religious freedom have emerged in recent months. He cautioned that many of these proposals extend beyond the immediate context of marriage issues, and parliament must approach them with care.

“Any reforms to protect religious freedom at large should be undertaken carefully,” Turnbull stated. He expressed concerns about the risk of unintended consequences when legislation is introduced to safeguard fundamental rights and freedoms, specifically mentioning freedom of religion. Moreover, the government aims to prevent uncertainties that may arise from broadly stated declarations akin to bill of rights-style legislation.

Turnbull asserted that Ruddock was well-qualified for this review due to his previous experience as Australia’s special envoy for human rights. The government expects that this expert assessment will serve as a valuable resource in contemplating any necessary legislative reforms regarding religious freedom.
